problem: Identical owner voice HTTP request after a two-second server clock advance regenerated occurred_at and failed durable journal admission.
fix: Explicit owner voice admission atomically persists first receipt in existing INGRESS_COMMITTED; exact scoped ingress replay uses stored timestamp, then passes unchanged strict ordinary admit. Canonical turn flows into respond, stop closure and after_response.
constraints: Canonical UUID voice session/message and private owner audience only
No project or observation binding accepted by receive-time resolver
Changed principal/session/text and erased ingress still fail
Existing execution lock and committed reply reuse unchanged
Fresh authentication and authority checks retained
No process cache, separate ledger, global clock freeze or client-supplied timestamp

validation.environment: Separate PostgreSQL 16.13, disposable DB, 256 MiB tmpfs container; controlled model/semantic ports, no production model/Hindsight calls.
coverage: Unchanged original HTTP +2s replay regression now passes
New DB connection retains first ingress and committed reply
Simultaneous first admissions choose one durable timestamp/event
Changed identity/content/context rejected and ordinary timestamp conflict remains
Erased ingress cannot be repopulated by retry
Parallel HTTP request does not execute model twice
Reconstructed runtime +2s serves same committed reply without new model call
One durable memory outbox document and one MEMORY_RETAIN_QUEUED event across retry
Canonical timestamp reaches stop and after_response

review.scope: Source plus final regression assertions reviewed; no remaining blocker.

limits: This is a bounded message-identity replay contract; recent/active_work/work_results are not durably fingerprinted as a complete HTTP payload.
Parallel in-flight duplicate may return conflict; it is not promised to wait for the first reply.
No new exactly-once provider execution claim across a crash during an uncommitted provider request.
Not deployed; no production restart, model call or cutover performed.
